title: The timer plasmoid lost functions to adjust individual digits of the time by scrolling over them
line: Scrolling over a digit of the Timer in the panel now changes that digit (hours, tens of minutes, minutes…) instead of always the seconds.
explanation: The Timer's compact view (panel, small desktop widget) draws the time as one text label with a single wheel handler for the whole applet, so every wheel step added or removed one second (or one minute without seconds) wherever the pointer was. Per-digit scrolling only existed in the full view's digit editor. The wheel handler now maps the pointer position onto the label's hh:mm:ss text and steps the hovered digit by its value (10 h, 1 h, 10 min, 1 min, 10 s, 1 s); over the icon, a colon or when the time is hidden it keeps the old seconds step.

commits.message:
applets/timer: scroll the hovered digit in the compact view

Scrolling over the time in the panel or a small desktop timer always
changed the seconds, wherever the pointer was. The wheel now finds the
digit under the pointer and steps it, like the full view's digits do.

BUG: 461285

media.caption: Master: timer at 00:00:00, three wheel notches over the tens of minutes, then three over the hours (red circle = pointer): only the seconds change.
With the fix, the same notches change the tens of minutes, then the hours.

reviews.text: Mapping wheel coordinates onto the compact label's hh:mm:ss characters cleanly restores per-digit scrolling in the panel and compact desktop view without complicating the layout. However, allowing large per-digit step sizes (up to 10 hours) exposes a rotation accumulation bug in adjustTime(): when scrolling up hits the 24-hour clamp, wheelHandler.rotation is never consumed, so subsequent scrolling on another digit (even scrolling down) can unexpectedly jump the timer upward. There are also minor edge-case gaps in digitStepAt() for zero contentWidth and RTL Text.AlignJustify alignment.
changes: In adjustTime(), consume or reset the wheel rotation value when the 24*60*60 upper clamp prevents incrementing (e.g. decrement value inside the while (value >= 15) loop regardless of whether seconds + stepsize < 24*60*60), so leftover rotation from scrolling tens-of-hours at >= 14:00:00 cannot leak into later scrolls on other digits.

In digitStepAt(), guard against contentWidth <= 0 before dividing and bound the loop by digitSteps.length, and account for RTL right alignment when effectiveHorizontalAlignment === Text.AlignJustify (e.g. when a title makes the label wider than contentWidth).
